# Refactor Requirements Quality Checklist: Node Event-Loop Refactor

**Purpose**: Validate that the 004 requirements (spec.md + clarifications, with plan.md as design context) are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable for a behavior-preserving refactor — i.e., that "parity" is fully enumerated and the structural contract is written precisely enough to implement and verify against
**Created**: 2026-06-09
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Behavioral-Parity Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are parity requirements enumerated for **all** public methods, or only the receive path and subscription surface? `send` (unregistered-recipient drop, sender/subscription decoupling), `id`, `peers`, `events`, and `spawn_producer` are absent from FR-001..007, and SC-004's parenthetical narrows the surface to "getter and subscribe/unsubscribe signatures and outcomes" [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-001..007, §SC-004]
  - **FAIL → resolved 2026-06-09**: added FR-015 (send parity: resolves on network accept, unregistered-recipient silent drop, sender/subscription decoupling) and widened SC-004's parenthetical to all public methods. `id`/`peers`/`events`/`spawn_producer` deliberately not given individual FRs — identity pass-throughs covered by the widened SC-004 + contracts/public-surface.md §A.
- [x] CHK002 Is the topic-filter-before-signature-verification **ordering** stated as a requirement (it is — FR-003) also reflected in an acceptance scenario, so a reviewer can trace it to an observable check? [Traceability, Spec §FR-003]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (maintainer decision)**: the observable contract is drop ⇒ absent from the received-messages snapshot (US1/US2 scenarios cover it). The ordering clause in FR-003 is an internal cost directive traced through data-model.md's transition table; no ordering-specific observability (e.g. verifier-interaction instrumentation) is added — not worth the granularity at this stage.
- [x] CHK003 Are the preserved **log event names and fields** (`message_dropped` + `cause`, subscription events) specified somewhere implementation-neutral enough to survive the refactor, given logs are explicitly not a test surface? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002/003/007; contracts/public-surface.md §A]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09**: FR-002/003/007 pin the semantics (causes, snake_case convention); contracts/public-surface.md §A pins the literal event names/fields with the explicit anti-silent-rename framing. Enforcement is the post-implementation review/analyze pass against contract §A — deliberately not automated, per the logs-are-operator-UX standard.
- [x] CHK004 Is "receive order" defined precisely enough under multiple concurrent producers (is it queue-arrival/event-processing order, with cross-producer interleaving explicitly unspecified)? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001, §US1-AS6]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only, no spec edit)**: "receive order" = event-processing order (= queue-arrival order; single queue, single consumer). Per-producer FIFO is guaranteed by the channel; cross-producer interleaving is unspecified and no requirement promises determinism there. Semantics unchanged from 003. Stated in data-model.md ("entries appear in event-processing order"); kept out of spec language to avoid importing the queue mechanism into a WHAT-level document.
- [x] CHK005 Is duplicate-delivery behavior (same message delivered twice) intentionally unaddressed as out-of-scope parity (003 has no dedup), and should that exclusion be recorded? [Coverage, Assumption, Gap]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: intentional. Parity baseline has no dedup — two identical deliveries yield two snapshot entries, preserved by the refactor ("no new protocol behavior is added"; FR-001 records every accepted delivery). Dedup is already tracked as future work at IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES N-005 (MessageHash as its anchor). No spec exclusion added — out-of-scope lists name near-term planned work (FR-013/014), not every absent feature.

## Structural-Contract Clarity & Measurability

- [x] CHK006 Is "pure" defined operationally in the requirements (no I/O / no concurrency / no asynchrony — FR-008) in a way consistent with the ambient-logging carve-out recorded only in Assumptions and ADR 0011? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008 vs §Assumptions]
  - **MINOR FAIL → resolved 2026-06-09**: FR-008's absolutist "no I/O" literally contradicted the inline ambient logging the Assumptions permit. Reworded FR-008 to "no protocol I/O" (ADR 0011's exact term) with an explicit pointer to the Assumptions carve-out. Pre-empts a spurious analyze finding against log emission inside the transition.
- [x] CHK007 Can FR-011 / SC-005 ("no producer may outlive the node", "no leaked background activity") be **objectively verified**, given task abort is asynchronous — is the intended observable (no further events recorded after drop) stated as the measurement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-011, §SC-005]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: SC-005 already states the effects-level observable (no further events recorded; no leaked background activity) — which is what abort guarantees and what can be checked. FR-011's "outlive" = ownership contract (every producer handle owned + aborted; nothing survives unboundedly), not instantaneous-abort atomicity. Verification is structural (Drop aborts all owned handles, per contracts §A Drop row) + the existing suite; no new instrumentation, consistent with the CHK002 ruling.
- [x] CHK008 Is the fate of events **already queued but unprocessed at drop** specified (discarded), or only the push-after-shutdown case? Flagged low-impact in clarify round 2; confirm SC-005's implication is sufficient or make it an explicit edge case [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, §SC-005]
  - **MINOR GAP → resolved 2026-06-09**: added an Edge Cases bullet — queued events are discarded with the queue at drop; teardown does not drain. Pure discard semantics (no new observability), parity with 003 teardown. Closes the one Outstanding item from clarify round 2.
- [x] CHK009 Does SC-003's measurability depend on an external feature's future work (008 adding its arm), and is there an in-feature verification (e.g., the no-op-producer Independent Test in US3) that suffices on its own? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, §US3]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: producer half verified in-feature by US3's no-op-producer test; event-kind half structurally reviewable (thin exhaustive match over named handlers — "one dispatch line + one handler, no edits to existing branches" checkable by inspection). The 008 parenthetical is a-posteriori confirmation, not a merge gate; this feature's gates are SC-001/002/004/005 + US scenarios, all in-feature.
- [x] CHK010 Are the **three seam items'** stability requirements (Event, EventQueue, events()/spawn_producer unchanged) stated as requirements rather than only implied by "no new public API"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010/012; contracts/public-surface.md §A]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: layered coverage — FR-010/012 require the capabilities the seam items provide; SC-004 (post-CHK001 widening) names producer registration explicitly; contracts §A pins exact signatures + the unchanged `pub use event::{Event, EventQueue}`; Assumptions bind to the seam contract doc whose §3 is the normative three-item list (cited by both features). No literal "seam MUST NOT change" FR added — would duplicate contract §A; the layering is the better structure.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Are spec FR-008's "crate-internal" wording, the Clarifications entry, SC-004, and contracts/public-surface.md §B mutually consistent on exactly **which** items are crate-internal (NodeState, apply, Effect, handlers) vs already-public seam items? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §Clarifications; contracts §B]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: all four sources agree. Corner case checked — `Effect`'s visibility is named only in contracts §B, but SC-004's categorical "no new public API is added" covers it transitively (a pub Effect would violate SC-004 literally, and would be unusable given crate-internal `apply`). Inverse direction also holds: the already-public seam items are nowhere swept into crate-internal wording (FR-010, contracts §A). Spec stays categorical, contract enumerates — same layering as CHK010.
- [x] CHK012 Do FR-013 ("transition returns no outbound commands") and FR-012 ("open to new event kinds without reshaping the contract") read consistently with the uninhabited-`Effect` decision — i.e., is it clear FR-013 constrains *this feature* and not the contract shape? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012/013]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: FR-013 is feature-scoped in every clause ("in this feature", "deferred to 004-connections"); FR-012's fixed "contract" is the signature, within which 008's event kind and 004-connections' effect variants are additive (`#[non_exhaustive]`, ADR 0011). Key Entities states the same scoping a third time. Empty-now / open-later is consistent everywhere it appears.
- [x] CHK013 Is the subscription model stated consistently across the spec — FR-004 (sync mutators preserved), Assumptions (config-seeded/static, registry-assumed-confirmed, future deprecation), and US1 acceptance scenarios exercising runtime subscribe — without implying a runtime-subscription *use case* this feature must newly support? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §Assumptions, §US1]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: three distinct roles that compose — FR-004 is parity (API preserved because 002/003 shipped it), the Assumption is operational (no production flow mutates; "only in tests"), and US1 scenarios 4–5 are exactly those tests. No scenario implies an operator/feature driving runtime changes; that future is routed to registry-driven events (008+) in Assumptions/ADR 0012, which impose nothing on this feature.

## Non-Functional & Dependency Coverage

- [x] CHK014 Are performance-parity expectations (refactor must not change receive-path asymptotics; one lock instead of two) intentionally confined to plan.md, or should the spec carry a non-functional parity requirement? [Gap, Non-Functional; plan.md Technical Context]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only, maintainer-confirmed)**: intentional confinement. A spec NFR would be unmeasurable (no benchmarks, no prior latency targets, in-process mock network) — an unquantified-adjective defect. What's assertable is structural and lives in plan.md / ADR 0012 (same per-event work, two locks → one). Constitutionally, optimization is not prioritised — Principle I values correctness over optimization, and no ROADMAP entry names a perf budget to trace to; first measurable perf surface arrives with a real transport (009).
- [x] CHK015 Is the dependency direction with 008 stated as a requirement (this feature defines the seam, must not consume registry concepts), so a reviewer can reject accidental `Registry`-aware code in 004? [Dependency, Spec §FR-014, §Assumptions]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: three layers — FR-014's MUST NOT (requirement gate), Assumptions' explicit direction ("this feature does not depend on 008"), and seam contract §3's grep-able criterion ("Feature A's branch never imports `Registry`") + ownership table. Also verified: data-model's "reserved, not added here" mention of RegistryUpdate is descriptive, not a stub license — the variant/payload are Feature B's to define.
- [x] CHK016 Are the merge-ordering obligations from the seam contract (004 lands first; whoever merges second writes the new arm) reflected or referenced in this feature's artifacts where a reviewer will see them? [Traceability, Dependency; event-loop-and-registry-contract.md §4]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: contract §4 is the normative source (cited by spec Assumptions + plan); research.md R1 and ADR 0011's consequences carry the obligation in-feature; CLAUDE.md ("Manual branch step" + SPECKIT block) states it for maintainers. The merges-second real-arm obligation correctly lives in the contract both features cite — it binds 008's (or 004-connections') review, not this feature's code.

- [x] CHK017 Does plan.md's Constitution Check still cite the correct FR range — it references "FR-001..014 (parity + structure)" while the amended spec now ends at FR-015? [Consistency, Traceability, plan.md §Constitution Check vs Spec §FR-015]

  - **Re-addressed same day**: CHK018's fix added FR-016, re-staling the range; bumped to FR-001..016 in the same walk.
- [x] CHK018 Is SC-004's widened parenthetical ("construction, send, … drop behavior") fully backed by requirements — construction parity (registration failure → typed error; no background activity leaked on failed construction) is named in SC-004 but covered by no FR or edge case [Coverage, Gap, Spec §SC-004]
  - **FAIL → resolved 2026-06-09**: added FR-016 (successful construction returns a ready node; failed construction surfaces the existing typed error and leaves no background activity). The no-leak-on-failure clause is the real regression guard — the refactor reorders exactly the constructor region where register-before-spawn ordering currently makes it true by accident. Plan FR range bumped alongside (see CHK017).
- [x] CHK019 Does new FR-015 trace to acceptance coverage — which existing scenarios/tests exercise send's three preserved behaviors (resolve-on-accept, unregistered-recipient silent drop, sender/subscription decoupling) under SC-001's umbrella? [Traceability, Spec §FR-015, §SC-001]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (FR-015)**: resolve-on-accept + unregistered-recipient drop explicitly tested (`tests/two_node_ping.rs:78–100`, send-to-ghost-id asserts Ok); sender/subscription decoupling exercised implicitly by the publisher-pattern tests (`multi_publisher.rs`, `filter_composition.rs`, `topic_filter.rs` incl. `own_emission_not_in_local_snapshot`). All under SC-001's pass-unmodified gate.
  - **FR-016 extension (maintainer decision)**: success path covered by the suite's 15 `Node::new` call sites; failure path (duplicate registration) has **zero** coverage anywhere and is CLI-unreachable (per-process in-memory networks). No test added in 004 — a new test inside the parity feature would contradict its no-new-behavior/no-new-tests framing and trigger consistency-cascade rewording. Deferred to **004-connections** as a proper integration test via **IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES N-006**; in 004, the failure clause is verified by structural review (register precedes spawn — nothing to leak), per the CHK007 ruling.

### Fresh-Angle Coverage

- [x] CHK020 Is US2-AS3's determinism claim ("same input sequence ⇒ same state") explicitly conditional on the injected verifier being deterministic, and is that dependency recorded as an assumption? [Assumption, Measurability, Spec §US2-AS3]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: the verifier is a field of the constructed state value, so the claim formally reads "same initial state (verifier included) + same events ⇒ same final state" — the dependency is inside the Given, not ambient. Verification is deterministic in every honest impl (pure predicate of key/bytes/signature; mock proven deterministic in mock_crypto_repro.rs; Ed25519 likewise at 011). The reproducible-tests constitutional standard polices test nondeterminism generally; apply contains no clock/randomness/scheduling. No Assumptions bullet added.
- [x] CHK021 Is FR-008's "single explicit state value" scoped precisely to **mutable** state, so the immutable peer set and the I/O handles legitimately remaining outside it cannot be read as violations? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008; data-model.md §Node]
  - **PASS 2026-06-09 (annotation only)**: FR-008 binds "the node's **mutable** state"; peers is static by 001's contract and the handles are I/O/runtime plumbing — nothing mutable-and-transition-relevant lives outside NodeState. Inverse checked: NodeState containing the immutable verifier doesn't contradict (all-mutable-inside ≠ only-mutable-inside; data-model annotates it as a service handle). data-model's field tables document the boundary per field. Forward note: 004-connections' live connection sinks also stay on the shell by design (ADR 0011) — same reading applies then.
- [x] CHK022 Is checklists/requirements.md (the spec-quality checklist, validated against the pre-amendment spec text) still accurate after the round-1 edits, or should it note re-validation? [Traceability, Process, checklists/requirements.md]
  - **PASS (substance) + meta-fix 2026-06-09**: re-ran every requirements.md item against the amended spec — all still pass (FR-015/016 testable behavior-level MUSTs; FR-008 rewording improved precision; scope/assumptions/scenarios unchanged or strengthened). Appended a dated re-validation note to requirements.md so its all-pass claim is anchored to the amended text.
